The task nevertheless emits an incorrect bits_per_byte: for a 10-byte source whose zero-byte BOS decodes as '<BOS>', it subtracts 5 nonexistent source bytes and returns 2.000000005 rather than 1.000000003, a concrete 2.000x error in the defined compression quantity.

COMPARABILITY/NORMALIZATION: bits_per_byte has a valid ordinary retokenization mechanism (PPL 2/4/16 became BPB 1.000000 within 1.7e-7), but it fails directly for zero-width control tokens by 2.000x and reduces rho(parameters) only -1.000 -> -0.800 while retaining rho(n_layers) = -0.894 and introducing rho(vocab_size) = +0.447; it must not be certified as an architecture-normalized twin.

DOC, perplexity.py:16-20: the class calls Python code points 'UTF-8 characters' and describes BPC as tokenizer-independent, while the code separately counts len(corpus) and len(corpus.encode('utf-8')); for ten U+00E9 characters those denominators are 10 versus 20 bytes, an exact 2.000x distinction that the class-level definition elides.
fix: Compute BPB from an exact token-to-source-byte coverage map: either prepend a valid BOS/EOS context so every source token is scored and divide by all source UTF-8 bytes, or request offsets/special-token masks and sum only byte spans of scored non-special targets; never subtract decode(first_id), and exclude every disjoint-window boundary target consistently. Materialize the selected rows once and reuse them for both passes, make every strided_perplexity return a 7-tuple, and fail closed (or emit an unprefixed protocol discriminator) instead of silently overwriting ppl_overall with the per-document fallback.
